headline: President Bush ended a national emergency first declared in 1986 under Executive Order 12543, which dealt with a foreign government's policies.
what_it_does: This order ends the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12543. That 1986 order dealt with the policies and actions of the government of Libya and was the basis for economic sanctions on that country. Ending the emergency removes the legal basis for sanctions that depended on it. The title is cut off and no summary was provided, so the details of which rules changed are not given here.

who_it_affects.group: US businesses and individuals dealing with Libya
who_it_affects.how: Trade and financial limits that relied on the 1986 emergency no longer have that legal basis once the emergency ends.

who_it_affects.group: People or entities whose property was frozen under the emergency
who_it_affects.how: Assets blocked under the emergency may no longer be held under that authority, though the source material does not spell out how.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed September 20, 2004; the exact effective date is not stated in the source material.
